paragraphs.text: Cyrus partly, but Christ principally {Mat 12:18} {See Trapp on "Mat 12:18"} {Php 2:7} A servant he was, yet not menial, but magisterial; that he was one or other is admirable, and well deserveth an Ecce Behold.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold my servant.

paragraphs.text: That he faint not under the weight of his Mediatorship, and the importable burden of my wrath, which he must suffer for a season. Some render it "whom I lean upon." See 2Ki 5:18; 2Ki 7:2; 2Ki 7:13.
paragraphs.anchor: Whom I uphold.

paragraphs.text: Cyrus was so. {Isa 43:10 Joh 6:27; Joh 6:29; Joh 10:36} See the notes on Mat 12:18. Cyrus was so singular a man, saith Herodotus, {a} that no Persian ever held himself worthy to be compared unto him. And of his court Xenophon {b} hath this memorable saying, that though a man should seek or choose blindfold, he could not miss of a good man. How much more truly may this be spoken of the Lord Christ and his people?
paragraphs.anchor: Mine elect, or choice one.

paragraphs.text: ευδοκησε. God affected Cyrus, {Isa 45:3-4; Isa 44:28} but nothing so well as Christ. {Mat 3:17; Mat 17:5} Once God repented him that he had made man; but now it is otherwise.
paragraphs.anchor: In whom my soul delighteth.

paragraphs.text: Who shall all cry, "Grace, grace unto it," to see mercy rejoicing against judgment. See on Mat 12:18.
paragraphs.anchor: He shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.

paragraphs.text: {a} Herod., lib. iii.
{b} Xenoph. Cyrop., lib. viii.

See on Mat 12:19. Cyrus was a very mild and gentle prince, so that his Persians called him their father, but his son, Cambyses, their lord, as Herodotus {a} recordeth. Christ’s government {b} is much more gentle; he will not by a loud and terrible voice frighten broken spirits, or rule them with rigour, &c. Christians must likewise put away all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour. And "be ye kind one to another, tender hearted." {Eph 4:31-32} This is to be like unto Christ - all whose actions, whether moral or mediatory, were either for our imitation or instruction.
paragraphs.anchor: He shall not cry, nor lift up.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. iii.
{b} Cyrus umbra, Christus Sol ipse.

i.e., A contrite heart, {Psa 51:17} in whom there shall appear to be anything of Christ, though never so little: that are faithful in weakness, though but weak in faith, as he was who cried out, Lord, I believe, help mine unbelief; {Mar 9:24} and another, Invoco te fide quamvis languida, fide tamen. {a} See on Mat 12:20.
paragraphs.anchor: A bruised reed shall he not break

paragraphs.text: Unto victory, saith the evangelist, after the Septuagint. Truth will prevail, sincerity proceed to perfection. "The righteous also shall hold on his way: and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger." {Job 17:9} Where there is truth of grace, there will be victory. Bernard never went from God without God. And holy Bradford would never give over any good duty till he found something coming in - as in confession, till his heart melted; in begging pardon, till it was quieted; in seeking grace, till it was quickened, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: He shall bring forth judgment unto truth.

paragraphs.text: {a} Cruciger.

Non erit tristis nec turbulentus; so the Vulgate hath it. He shall be master of his passions, and keep an even state of his looks and motions, whatever befall, as they report of Socrates. He shall not knit his brows, or chide - which was Eli’s fault, {1Sa 3:13} but is Christ’s commendation - so Lud. de Dieu rendereth it. He shall not make to smoke (so Junius from Isa 42:3), nor shall he bruise any one.
paragraphs.anchor: He shall not fail, nor be discouraged.

paragraphs.text: See on Isa 42:3.
paragraphs.anchor: Until he have set judgment.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Shall with desire expect his doctrine.
paragraphs.anchor: And the isles shall wait for his law.

paragraphs.text: Heb., And they that stretched them out; noting the Trinity in unity. {as Deu 6:4} Some pagans concluded the world must needs have had a beginning, otherwise we could not know whether the egg or the bird, the seed or the plant, the day or the night, the light or the darkness, were first.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus saith God the Lord, he that created the heavens, and stretched them out.

paragraphs.text: To the Mediatorship.
paragraphs.anchor: I the Lord have called thee.

paragraphs.text: Working wonders by thee, and with thee.
paragraphs.anchor: And will hold thine hand.

paragraphs.text: That thou be not crucified till thine hour be come, and that thou despair not when thou sufferest.
paragraphs.anchor: And will keep thee.

paragraphs.text: i.e., For that "angel of the covenant," {Mal 3:1} and that thou mayest reconcile all the elect in one body to me by thy cross, &c. {Eph 2:16}
paragraphs.anchor: And give thee for a covenant of the people

paragraphs.text: See Isa 9:2.
paragraphs.anchor: For a light to the Gentiles.

paragraphs.text: By the preaching of the gospel. {Act 26:18 2Co 4:4-6 Rev 3:18}
paragraphs.anchor: To open the blind eyes.

paragraphs.text: To free poor souls from the tyranny of sin and terror of hell. This should make us say to Christ, as one did once to Augustus for a deliverance nothing so great, Effecisti, Ceesar, ut viverem et morerer ingratus, Let me do mine utmost, I must live and die in thy debt.
paragraphs.anchor: To bring out the prisoners from the prison.

paragraphs.text: I, and no heathen petty god, as I have plainly and plentifully proved, nemine contradicente.
paragraphs.anchor: I am the Lord.

paragraphs.text: God, though he be above all name (when Manoah inquired after his name, the answer was, It is wonderful - i.e., far above thy conception), yet here we have his proper name, Jehovah, which is also called his glory, because incommunicable to any creature.
paragraphs.anchor: That is my name.

paragraphs.text: To his Son Christ he hath given it, {Joh 17:2} who, although he is Alius, another yet he is not Aliud different from the Father, but of the same nature and essence. God hath given being to all things, life to many, sense to others, reason to men and angels, his glory he will not give to any. Excellently hereupon Bernard, {a} My glory I will not, &c.; what then wilt thou give us, Lord? what wilt thou give us? My peace, saith he, I give you; my peace I leave unto you. It is enough for me, Lord; I thankfully take what thou leavest, and leave what thou keepest to thyself, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: And my glory will I not give to another.

paragraphs.text: {a} Serm. xiii. in Cant.
The prophecies are fulfilled.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, the former things are come to pass.

paragraphs.text: Therefore I am the true God undoubtedly, and the doctrine of my prophets is true assuredly, veriora quam quae ex tripode. Siquidem Satan etsi semel videatur verax, millies est mendax, et semper fallax.
paragraphs.anchor: Before they spring forth, I tell you of them.

paragraphs.text: The disputation being ended, and God having clearly got the better, the prophet singeth this gratulatory song, and calleth upon others to bear a part with him therein, and especially for Christ and his benefits before mentioned.
paragraphs.anchor: Sing unto the Lord a new song.

paragraphs.text: i.e., That dwell toward the west of Judea.
paragraphs.anchor: Ye that go down to the sea

paragraphs.text: Ye that dwell eastward. It was called the wilderness, because but thinly inhabited.
paragraphs.anchor: Let the wilderness.

paragraphs.text: The most fierce and savage people, cicurated and civilised by the gospel preached among them, as it is with us at this day, whose ancestors were most barbarous and brutish, as Cicero {a} testifieth.
paragraphs.anchor: The villages that Kedar doth inhabit.

paragraphs.text: Or, Of Petra, the chief city of Arabia Petraea.
paragraphs.anchor: Let the inhabitants of the rock.

paragraphs.text: {a} De Nat. Deor.
See Isa 42:10.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them give glory.

paragraphs.text: Or, As a giant. And here, by an elegant hypotyposis, {a} the fierce wrath of God against his foes is set forth to the life, and appointed also to be sung for a second part of the ditty - viz., Christ’s conquest over sin, death, and hell, whereby we are made "more than conquerors."
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man.

paragraphs.text: Iubilabit atque etiam barriet; he shall make a hideous and horrible noise, such as the Roman soldiers did of old when they began the battle, and as the Turks do at this day on purpose to frighten their enemies. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: He shall cry, yea, roar.

paragraphs.text: {a} Vivid description of a scene, event, or situation, bringing it, as it were, before the eyes of the hearer or reader.
{b} Vegetius.

As a travailing woman biteth in her pain as long as she is able. So had God, for causes best known to himself, forborne a long while to appear for his people and to avenge them of their enemies. But now Patientia laesa fit furor: Deique patientia quo diuturnior, est minacior. Now down goeth Dagon and the devil’s whole kingdom before this jealous giant.
paragraphs.anchor: I have long time holden my peace.

paragraphs.text: Which when she can bear no longer, sets up her note, and is heard all the house over. This is very comfortable. God is pained, as it were, for his people - in all their afflictions he is afflicted; he longs for their deliverance, which therefore shall not be long ere it come.
paragraphs.anchor: Now will I cry like a travailing woman.

paragraphs.text: I will rather invert the order of nature, and mingle heaven and earth together, than my Church shall want seasonable help. I will also remove all obstacles by sending fire upon the earth, {Luk 12:49} and bring every high thought into a holy obedience. {2Co 10:5}
paragraphs.anchor: I will make waste mountains and hills.

paragraphs.text: This was fulfilled, in the letter, to the Jews brought back from Babylon, where they had been close prisoners, and, in the mystery, to all Christ’s converts - more especially to that blind boy presented to Bishop Hooper, martyr, the day before his death, at Gloucester, where the boy had not long before suffered imprisonment for confessing the truth. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will bring the blind by a way.

paragraphs.text: By bringing them out of darkness into my marvellous light. {1Pe 2:9}
paragraphs.anchor: I will make darkness light before.

paragraphs.text: {a} Acts and Mon.

Heb., Be ashamed with shame; because disappointed and defeated, as the Papists oft have been when they have fought against Protestants, in that Bellum Hussiticum in Germany especially; and yet Bellarmine hath the face to say that the Catholics were never yet worsted by the heretics, as they call us, in a set battle.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall be greatly ashamed.

paragraphs.text: Ye who, as so many sea monsters or deaf adders, will not hear, and as so many blind moles will not see, by a petulant blindness, and of obstinate malice; such were the scribes and Pharisees, who winked hard with their eyes, and wilfully shut the windows, lest the light should come in unto them. See more of this in the notes on Isa 6:1-13 Isa 29:1-24.
paragraphs.anchor: Hear, ye deaf; and look, ye blind.

paragraphs.text: In nature, Caecorum mens occulatissima est. We read of Didymus Alexandrinus, that though blind, yet he wrote commentaries; and of two of Archbishop Ussher’s aunts, that being blind from their cradles, they taught him first to read, such was their readiness in the Scriptures. But this was rare; and in spirituals it is otherwise, till God enlighten both organ and object.
paragraphs.anchor: That ye may see.

paragraphs.text: Who so blind as he that will not see? Israel was God’s peculiar, and had the light of his law, yet were blind as beetles.
paragraphs.anchor: Who is blind, but my servant?

paragraphs.text: The priests and Levites. {Mal 2:7} Such were the Papist dolts till awakened by the Reformation.
paragraphs.anchor: Or deaf, as my messenger?

paragraphs.text: The elders of the people, who arrogated to themselves perfection {a} {Isa 65:5 Rom 2:17-20} as likewise the Popish perfectists, the Jewish doctors with their pretended Mashlamnuthas, and the Turkish Mussulmans - i.e., perfectionaries.
paragraphs.anchor: Who is blind as he that is perfect?

paragraphs.text: {a} Buxtorf. Tiber. p. 5.
viz., For holy practice.
paragraphs.anchor: But observest not

paragraphs.text: viz., For any good purpose, he heareth not "what the Spirit saith to the churches."
paragraphs.anchor: But he heareth not.

paragraphs.text: Or, To magnify his law and make it honourable - sc., by recompensing so highly those that observed it; this he did for his "righteousness’ sake" - i.e., of his free grace and fidelity; but these are none such, they are practical Antinomians, and to me to the diametrically opposite.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord is well pleased; he will magnify his law, &c.

paragraphs.text: And all too little, unless they were better. Jerome expoundeth this of the destruction of the Jews by the Romans, after their voluntary blindness and malice showed against Christ, at what time they were pulled out of holes and privies, spoiled, slaved, sold thirty a penny.
paragraphs.anchor: But this is a people robbed and spoiled.

paragraphs.text: Magna nimirum haec sunt, sed paucis persuasa. We shall have much ado to make you believe these things, though your liberties, lives, and souls lie upon it.
paragraphs.anchor: Who among you will give ear to this?

paragraphs.text: Omnia magno adfectu sunt pronuncianda, debentque singula membra huius orationis expendi. This is a very remarkable passage. Let us cry out, "Oh the severity!" and beware. Cavebimus autem si pavebimus. Moreover, we will beware if we are terrified.
paragraphs.anchor: Who gave Jacob for a spoil?

paragraphs.text: When the country was wasted, the city and temple burnt and ruined. Read Josephus, Lege, inquam, et luge. I say read and weep.
paragraphs.anchor: And it hath set him on fire.

paragraphs.text: This was worse than all the rest. Like a sleepy man (fire burning in his bed straw) he crieth not out, when others haply lament his case, that see afar off, but cannot help him.
paragraphs.anchor: And he laid it not to heart.
